::: {.callout-note}
This is a living essay under active development. Every chapter will be backed by a reproducible Colab notebook and at least one controlled experiment.
:::

> **Thesis.** Model capability is not produced by architecture alone. Data, compute allocation, optimization, adaptation, modality interfaces, inference strategy, and evaluation form one coupled system.

## What the reader will build

- A small pre-training data-cleaning and packing pipeline
- A Transformer compute and memory estimator
- A toy MoE router plus LoRA and model-soup experiments
- A miniature vision-language alignment pipeline
- A toy diffusion model with a visual denoising trajectory
- A prompt and evaluation harness with confidence intervals

## Chapter 1 · Data becomes model behavior

### History and theory
<!-- Curated corpora → web-scale mixtures → filtering, deduplication, contamination, synthetic data. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Sampling weights, token budgets, repetition, effective data size, and compute estimates. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Clean, deduplicate, tokenize, mix, and pack a small multi-domain corpus. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Data quality, duplication rate, and mixture weights versus validation loss. -->

### Failure analysis and interview takeaways
<!-- Leakage, benchmark contamination, PII, memorization, and irreproducible recipes. -->

## Chapter 2 · Scaling training without losing control

### History and theory
<!-- DDP, FSDP/ZeRO, tensor, pipeline, context, and expert parallelism. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Parameters, gradients, optimizer state, activations, communication, and MFU. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Build a compute/memory estimator; demonstrate accumulation and checkpointing. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Sequence length, microbatch size, precision, checkpointing, memory, and step time. -->

## Chapter 3 · Sparse models and efficient adaptation

### History and theory
<!-- Switch Transformer, Mixtral, fine-grained MoE, LoRA, QLoRA, merging, model soups. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Router probability, balance loss, active parameters, low-rank ΔW = BA, averaging assumptions. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Train a toy router and two adapters; merge them using several soup weights. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Expert collapse, top-k, capacity, LoRA rank, and interpolation weight. -->

## Chapter 4 · Extending language models to vision

### History and theory
<!-- ViT, CLIP, Flamingo, LLaVA, visual tokens, projectors, resamplers, cross-attention. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Patch embeddings, contrastive loss, cross-attention, and multimodal token budgets. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Implement patchify + encoder + projector, or train a miniature CLIP. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Patch size, projector depth, frozen versus trainable encoders, attention maps. -->

## Chapter 5 · Diffusion and generative media

### History and theory
<!-- VAE/GAN → DDPM → latent diffusion → DiT → flow matching. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Forward noising, epsilon/v prediction, CFG, schedulers, flow-matching intuition. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Train a toy DDPM and visualize its denoising trajectory. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Sampling steps, scheduler, guidance, seed, quality, and latency. -->

## Chapter 6 · Prompt optimization and honest evaluation

### History and theory
<!-- Zero/few-shot, CoT, self-consistency, ReAct, prompt search, modality-specific controls. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Accuracy, pass@k, Elo/Bradley–Terry, bootstrap CI, FID, and judge bias. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Build one harness for prompt variants, pairwise comparisons, and reports. -->

### Model landscape
<!-- Family, evolution, public architecture facts, strengths, weaknesses, and benchmarks. -->

## Reproducibility checklist

- [ ] Data sources, filters, and sampling weights are documented
- [ ] Compute and memory estimates state their assumptions
- [ ] Adapter and soup checkpoints share a compatible base
- [ ] Every multimodal experiment reports its token budget
- [ ] Generative comparisons control seeds and sampling settings
- [ ] Benchmark claims include dates, versions, and primary sources
- [ ] Confidence intervals and failure cases accompany headline metrics
